html:
SMTO-FIL-0060 — SMTO couldn't open this compressed file

GUID: 86aa07a0-7402-50e8-82c8-4007478eb1ff
Slug: attachment-archive-format
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • The attached file isn't a ZIP, TAR or .gz file that SMTO can read, or it's damaged. SMTO didn't read anything from inside it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On your own computer, try opening the file with your usual unzip tool to check that it isn't damaged. A file that was cut off while downloading or copying can't be opened by anyone.
  2. If it's another kind of compressed file, such as .rar or .7z, unpack it on your computer and save the contents as a new .zip file. SMTO can read only ZIP, TAR and gzip (.gz, .tar.gz) files.
  3. Select the + (Add context) button in the message box to attach the working copy, then ask SMTO to look inside it again. SMTO needs a readable copy before it can list or read the files inside.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the files inside the compressed file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and where it came from, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Archive inspection failed: the attachment is not a recognizable ZIP, uncompressed TAR or gzip file, or its ZIP end-of-central-directory record is missing or corrupt.

What this means

  • ZIP/TAR/Gzip recognition or bounded parsing failed. The exact receipt distinguishes unsupported archive structure from corrupt or unreadable compressed data. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • ZIP/TAR/Gzip recognition or bounded parsing failed. The exact receipt distinguishes unsupported archive structure from corrupt or unreadable compressed data.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Test the source with unzip -t, tar -tf or gzip -t; replace a truncated copy, and convert unsupported formats (rar, 7z, bz2- or xz-compressed tar) to ZIP or TAR/gzip. The error's reason text says whether the ZIP directory is missing or corrupt or the format is unsupported; corrupt compressed data inside a recognized archive is reported as archive_corrupt instead.
  • Use a valid supported ZIP, TAR or Gzip source; replace a damaged copy. Inspect the retained parser reason before retrying.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Bounded inspection returns member metadata without extracting paths.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
